label: Radio
title: Radio
summary: Use a Radio to pick exactly one option from a short list, such as the account to pay from or how often to invest.
corePrinciple: One choice from a visible set. Put a label beside every Radio, and let the whole row select it.

anatomy.title: A ring that fills when chosen
anatomy.description: Radio is an 18 px circle. Unselected it is a white ring; selected it fills purple and shows a white dot.
blocks: A 1 px deep-purple border outlines the circle.
A 10 px white dot confirms the choice.

anatomy.note: A 1 px deep-purple border outlines the circle.
A 10 px white dot confirms the choice.

configuration.title: Place it beside its label
configuration.description: Radio has no label of its own. Use list rows when options need detail, and a plain label for short options.
blocks: For options with detail, such as accounts. The whole row selects its Radio.
For short options. Only the circle responds to a press: 18 px in a browser, 44 px on phones.

examples.title: In list rows
examples.description: For options with detail, such as accounts. The whole row selects its Radio.

examples.title: Beside a short label
examples.description: For short options. Only the circle responds to a press: 18 px in a browser, 44 px on phones.

states.title: Selected, unselected, and disabled
states.description: The screen sets which Radio is selected and which are disabled. Hover adds a lilac glow; keyboard focus adds a yellow ring and an orange border.
blocks: Purple fill with a white dot.
Grey and not pressable, for an option that is unavailable now.

examples.title: Selected
examples.description: Purple fill with a white dot.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: Grey and not pressable, for an option that is unavailable now.

sizing.title: An 18 px circle inside a larger row
sizing.description: The Radio is always 18 × 18 px. On its own only the circle is pressable (44 px on phones, 18 px in a browser), so put it in a list row whose whole height and width select it.

content.title: Short, parallel options
content.description: Write options in sentence case with the same grammar, so they read as one set. Lead with the word that tells them apart, and keep two to five options visible.

inContext.title: Choosing the account to pay from
inContext.description: The screen keeps the chosen account, passes selected to each Radio, and enables Continue once one is chosen. Pressing a row or its Radio selects it.

doDont.title: One choice, clearly labelled
doDont.description: Each pair shows a set people can answer quickly versus one that confuses them.
blocks: One filled Radio shows the single answer.
Radio has no group, so the screen must stop a second selection.
Each option says what it is.
Without labels people can’t tell the options apart.
Use a Checkbox for yes or no
A Checkbox can be ticked and cleared.
Once chosen, a single Radio can’t be cleared.

sources.title: Use the public Radio contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository. Figma has eight variants (Idle, Hover, Active, Focus, and Disabled, unselected and selected); the package sets selected and disabled, and draws hover and focus itself. RadioButton is a deprecated name for the same component. Radio has no label or group: the screen keeps one selected value. On the web a Radio is announced as a radio button with its selected state, Space selects it, and the focused unselected border is Figma’s orange. Developers name each Radio with accessibilityLabel.
